docs.text: Classes All five classes follow one company: Cordillera Mobile , a mobile carrier that has just hired you as an analyst. Two teams bring you questions. The commercial team asks what drives a customer's monthly bill? The retention team asks which customers are about to cancel, and whom should we call? Each class moves that analysis one step forward, and that step is exactly the one your team takes that week in its own project. You watch it done with Cordillera on Wednesday or Friday, then do the same with your case and hand it in on Tuesday. Session 1 Day one at Cordillera Mobile Python in Colab, from a single customer to thousands at once with NumPy. We open the raw customer file for the first time. → Advance 1 · team, data, and question Session 2 Cleaning the customer base pandas and seaborn. We find every problem in the data, fix it with decisions we can defend, and find the first patterns. → Advance 2 · cleaning and exploratory analysis Session 3 What drives the monthly bill? Linear regression. Train and test, coefficients a manager can read, MAE, RMSE, R², overfitting, and cross-validation. → Advance 3 · ready to model Session 4 Who is about to leave? Logistic regression. The accuracy trap, the confusion matrix, and a threshold chosen with money instead of habit. → Advance 4 · the right metric Session 5 Better models, a clearer story Decision trees, random forests, ROC curves, and turning the results into a presentation with the pyramid principle . → Final project How to use a class Every class runs in your browser . Press ▶ next to a cell (or Shift + Enter ), edit the code and run it again; cells share variables, as in Colab. The animated explainers inside each class respond when you drag, slide, or press play, and the Check yourself questions tell you right away whether you got the idea. Browser or Colab? The browser is the quickest way to follow a class: nothing to install, nothing to save, and the first run takes a few seconds while Python downloads. For the project , work in Colab, where your notebook is saved and shared with your team ( Colab guide ). To open a class in Colab, use the Open in Colab button at the top of the class. The data is in Datasets : cordillera_mobile.csv (raw, as it arrives in session 1) and cordillera_mobile_clean.csv (after the session 2 cleaning). Reference These notebooks come from the semester edition of the course. They are not part of the classes, but they cover some topics in more depth if you want to go further. Notebook Topic Colab Introduction to Python Python syntax, data structures, functions NumPy Arrays, functions, indexing pandas Series, DataFrames, merging, dates Visualization with seaborn seaborn basics Linear regression Hospital length of stay: OLS, assumptions, diagnostics Underfitting and overfitting Polynomial regression Cross-validation Housing prices: RFE and k-fold Logistic regression and error metrics Travel package purchases Decision trees and random forests Travel package purchases, tuning, ROC Topics outside the intensive format (statistical inference, hypothesis testing, bootstrapping, ridge and lasso, nonlinear regression, SVMs) are in the semester course .

docs.text: Weekly progress The project moves forward every week . Each class takes the Cordillera Mobile analysis one step further, and your team then takes the same step with its own case and hands it in as an advance . There are four graded advances, and the fifth week ends with the final submission. How it counts Weekly advances: 30% of the course grade (4 advances, 7.5% each). Final project: 70% (notebook and presentation, graded with the rubric ). Calendar Every advance is due on Tuesday at 23:59 , the same for both sections, and is submitted through the team mailbox . Week Session (Wed / Fri) Advance Due Feedback in 1 Python in Colab (Oct 28 / 30) Advance 1 · Team, data, and question Tue Nov 3 Session 2 2 pandas and seaborn (Nov 4 / 6) Advance 2 · Cleaning and exploratory analysis Tue Nov 10 Session 3 3 Linear regression (Nov 11 / 13) Advance 3 · Ready to model Tue Nov 17 Session 4 4 Classification (Nov 18 / 20) Advance 4 · The right metric Tue Nov 24 Session 5 5 Trees and communication (Nov 25 / 27) Final project Tue Dec 1 Presentation 6 Presentations (Dec 2 / 4) — — — How advances are graded Each advance is graded from 1.0 to 7.0 against its checklist. You get the grade and a traffic light, with comments in your notebook, during the next session's workshop. Grade Traffic light What it means 6.0 – 7.0 🟢 Every item is done and correct. Keep going. 4.0 – 5.9 🟡 Every item is there, but some need fixing before the next advance. 2.0 – 3.9 🔴 Important items are missing. We talk during the workshop. 1.0 ⚫ Not submitted. The notebook is reviewed as it is at the deadline . Colab keeps the version history, so later changes don't count for that advance (but they do help the next one). Late submissions: one point off for each day late, up to three days. After that the advance gets a 1.0. Every member of the team gets the same grade. If a member does not take part, let me know before the deadline. Each advance is a step towards the final notebook, so fixing the comments from one advance is part of the next. Advance 1 · Team, data, and question Work on it in the session 1 workshop. Due Tuesday, November 3, 23:59 . Modeled in class: Day one at Cordillera Mobile does every step below with Cordillera Mobile. Your team repeats it with its own case. Team registered in the mailbox (2 or 3 members, team name, and case). If it is your own case, include the proposal: it is approved or rejected in the feedback. Project notebook created in Colab and shared with the whole team (Editor) and with hizocar@gmail.com (Commenter). The data is loaded from its URL with pd.read_csv . First inspection: shape , data types, first rows, number of missing values per column, and number of duplicate rows. The case's business question, written in your own words in two or three lines, and who would use the answer. Advance 2 · Cleaning and exploratory analysis Work on it in the session 2 workshop. Due Tuesday, November 10, 23:59 . Modeled in class: Cleaning the customer base does every step below with Cordillera Mobile. Your team repeats it with its own case. Duplicates removed and missing values handled, with each decision justified. Inconsistent categories unified (for example, "bachelor" , "Bachelor" , and "BACHELOR" ). Impossible values (negative ages, scores out of range) detected and fixed. Cleaning summary table: issue, decision, and rows affected. At least four exploratory charts, including how the variables relate to the target. One sentence under each chart saying what it shows. Three written findings, each with what it means for the business. Advance 3 · Ready to model Work on it in the session 3 workshop. Due Tuesday, November 17, 23:59 . Modeled in class: What drives the monthly bill? does every step below with Cordillera Mobile. Your team repeats it with its own case. Categorical variables encoded (for example, with pd.get_dummies ) and ID columns removed. Data split into training and test sets before any model is trained. The test set is not touched until evaluation. Case A: linear regression trained, with MAE, RMSE, and R² on the test set, and the training metrics next to them to check for overfitting. Case B: split stratified by default , and the baseline accuracy of a model that always predicts "repays". Explain in two lines why accuracy alone would be misleading here. A short paragraph: what you expect the model to find, based on your exploratory analysis. Advance 4 · The right metric Work on it in the session 4 workshop (modeling clinic). Due Tuesday, November 24, 23:59 . Modeled in class: Who is about to leave? does every step below with Cordillera Mobile. Your team repeats it with its own case. Case A: 5-fold cross-validation for the linear regression, at least two coefficients interpreted in business terms, and a justified choice between MAE and RMSE. Case B: logistic regression with its confusion matrix, precision, recall, F1, and AUC on the test set. A decision threshold chosen and justified with the cost of each type of error. A table with the metrics so far, which will be extended in the final submission. The key message of your presentation in one sentence (the top of the pyramid). It can still change. Final submission Work on it in the session 5 workshop. Due Tuesday, December 1, 23:59 . Modeled in class: Better models, a clearer story does every step below with Cordillera Mobile. Your team repeats it with its own case. Second model (decision tree or random forest) trained and evaluated on the same split. Model comparison table and a justified choice. Feature importance for the chosen model, explained for the business. Three recommendations and the limitations of the analysis. A 10-minute presentation with a pyramid structure. Checklist from the Colab guide completed. Notebook submitted through the mailbox , and slides emailed as described in the project brief .

docs.text: Final project How the course is graded You work on one project for the whole course. It is graded in two parts: Weekly advances, 30%: four advances, one after each content session. See weekly progress . Final project, 70%: the finished notebook and the presentation, graded with the rubric below. Course grade = 0.3 × average of the advances + 0.7 × final project. Goal Solve a business problem with data, end to end, in a Google Colab notebook. The project has to show the four skills of the course: Skill What we expect to see Python in Colab A clean notebook that runs from start to finish without errors. Data analysis Clean data, documented data quality issues, and an exploratory analysis with findings. Models At least two trained models, evaluated on test data and compared with the right metric. Communication Concrete recommendations for the business, presented in 10 minutes. Teams 2 or 3 members , from the same section. Teams and cases are registered in the team mailbox at the end of session 1 (October 28 or 30). Cases Each team chooses one of these cases. The data is "dirty" on purpose: cleaning it is part of the job. Case A · TalentCo (regression) Case B · FinTrust Bank (classification) Case C · Your own case What drives an employee's salary? TalentCo suspects its pay structure is inconsistent: people with similar experience earn different amounts depending on their department, region, or education level. The people team wants to know which variables explain salary and whether there are gaps to fix. Data: employee_compensation.csv , about 10,000 rows and 9 columns. Target variable: Salary (annual salary in USD). Minimum models: linear regression and a tree-based model ( DecisionTreeRegressor or RandomForestRegressor ). Metrics: MAE, RMSE, and R² on test data. Which customers will not repay their loan? FinTrust's default rate keeps rising. The risk team wants a model that flags applicants who are likely to default before their loan is approved. Data: loan_default.csv , about 10,000 rows and 16 columns. Target variable: default (1 = defaulted, 0 = repaid). Minimum models: logistic regression and a tree-based model ( DecisionTreeClassifier or RandomForestClassifier ). Metrics: confusion matrix, precision, recall, F1, and AUC. Justify which one matters most, considering the cost of approving someone who defaults versus rejecting someone who would have repaid. You can propose a different problem with public data (for example, from Kaggle or a government open data portal) if it meets these conditions: At least 1,000 rows and a clear target variable (numeric or categorical). A business question that a model can answer. The data can be read from a public URL. Your own case must be approved in Advance 1 . What the notebook must contain Context and business question. What problem you are solving and for whom. Loading and describing the data. Size, variable types, and a short data dictionary. Cleaning. Duplicates, missing values, inconsistent categories, and impossible values. A summary table with each issue, the decision you made, and how many rows it affected. Exploratory analysis. At least four relevant charts, each with one sentence explaining what it shows. Close with 3 to 5 findings. Preparing for modeling. Encoding categorical variables and splitting into training and test sets. Models. At least two models, evaluated on the same test split. Comparison and choice. A table with each model's metrics and a justification for the model you choose. Interpretation. Which variables matter most in the model and what that means for the business. Recommendations. Three concrete actions the company could take, and the limitations of your analysis. Submission What When How Colab notebook Tuesday, December 1, 23:59 Team mailbox , choosing Final project Notebook ( .ipynb ) and slides (PDF) Tuesday, December 1, 23:59 Email to hizocar@gmail.com with the subject [ML Intensive] Final project – Section – Team name Presentation, Casa Central Wednesday, December 2, 16:05 In the classroom Presentation, Vitacura Friday, December 4, 11:05 In the classroom The presentation lasts 10 minutes plus 5 for questions , and every team member must take part. The presentation order is published on Monday, November 30. Rubric This rubric gives the final project grade (70% of the course). The weights below add up to 100% of that grade. Criterion Weight Full marks (7.0) Python and reproducibility 15% The notebook runs end to end with Restart session and run all . The code is tidy, with headings and text explaining each step. The data is read from a URL. Cleaning and exploratory analysis 25% Data quality issues are found and fixed, and each decision is justified. Charts are relevant and each one has a conclusion. Findings connect to the business question. Modeling and evaluation 30% At least two models with a training and test split and no data leakage. The chosen metric fits the problem. The comparison is fair and the choice is well argued. Interpretation and recommendations 15% You explain which variables matter and how. Recommendations are concrete, follow from the results, and acknowledge limitations. Oral presentation 15% Pyramid structure: the conclusion comes first. Clear charts, stays within 10 minutes, everyone takes part, and questions are answered well. Grades use the Chilean scale from 1.0 to 7.0, where 4.0 is a pass. Advances and the final grade are connected Each advance is a piece of the final notebook. The comments you get on an advance are the fastest way to raise the final grade: fix them before the next one, and you reach December without surprises.
